applies_to: VersiCharge AC series chargers with firmware V2.135 or later (per-register minimum firmware is given in the source).
summary: The Siemens VersiCharge AC wallbox has a Modbus server on both RS-485 (RTU) and Ethernet (TCP) once Modbus is enabled for the charger in the cloud configuration. Everything is a holding register. This map covers identity and hardware data, the J1772 and OCPP state, error codes, per-phase current, voltage, power, power factor and energy, the Modbus charging-current limit with its fallback current and timeout and the reset/address registers.

addressing.note: The map prints every register four ways: 'external' decimal (40001 style), 'internal' decimal, and both in hex. External 40001 is internal 0, so the internal number is the wire address: external 41634 = internal 1633 = 0x661. 'documented' below is the external number; 'address' is the internal one. The map's own notes mix the two (it cites both 'register 1633' and 'register 41661'), so check which one is meant.

source.title: VERSICHARGE AC SERIES ModBus Map
source.pages: p. 1 (port settings and notes), pp. 2-15 (register map)

notes: The energy counter (1692) is marked 'Uint32 (Big-endian)' in the map, so the high word comes first (ABCD).

Charging current limit (internal 1633): written values of 100 or less are whole amps, values 101-8000 are hundredths of an amp (write 6 or 600 for 6 A, 850 for 8.5 A). A read always returns whole amps in the 0-80 range. Values above 8000 are rejected, and anything under 6 A pauses charging. Other limits (OCPP smart charging, cloud power level) still apply on top.
Left out: the charging session energy target (internal 1640). Its units column says watt-hours but its description talks about kWh, so the scale cannot be settled from the map.
Production date (5-6): only the first word (year) is listed; the second packs month and day as two bytes.

Not listed: the five-register firmware strings for the M0 processor, the firmware variant and release-date strings, RFID card add/remove and whitelist blocks (40081-40338, 41853-41878) and the factory-reset salt/command registers, which are marked for internal use.
The map warns that when the charger is controlled by OCPP, Modbus is mainly a monitoring interface.

integration.summary: Poll internal 1599-1602 for state and faults and 1647-1677 for live values with function 3. To manage load, set the fallback current (1660) and fallback time (1661) once after every reboot, then write the charging current limit to 1633 inside that time window.
integration.enable: The charger must be commissioned (register 27 shows the link used), and the 'Modbus' setting must be True in the charger's VersiCloud group; otherwise the Modbus application does not start.
integration.watchdog: If Modbus traffic stops for the Fallback Time (1661, 0 or 60-600 s), the charger applies the Fallback Current Phase Sum (1660). Both registers reset at power cycle or Modbus soft reset and must be written again.
quirks: Registers are documented as 40001-style external numbers next to internal (wire) numbers; use the internal number in the request.
Supported functions: 03 read, 06 and 16 write (per register as listed in the map).
The charging current limit accepts amps or hundredths of amps depending on the size of the value written, but always reads back in amps.
Dynamic values may take several poll cycles to update after a change.
setup: RTU: 38400 baud, 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit, default address 2 (change at internal 1825, about 20 s to apply; write 1 to 1878 to restore 2).
Minimum timeout setting 10 s and minimum poll interval 5 s on both transports.
gotchas: A soft reset (write 1 to 1826) restarts the Modbus application, which takes about 60 s to come back.
Fallback current and fallback time are not persistent; re-write them after every reboot or soft reset.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
